exposure: BMI categories (normoweight, overweight, obesity type I, obesity type II, obesity type III)
cohort: 5871 women who gave birth between 2013 and 2018 in Spain
finding: Women with a higher BMI had a significantly increased risk of obstetric complications, including cephalopelvic disproportion, preeclampsia, labor induction, emergency cesarean section, overall morbidity in childbirth, and macrosomia.
mod_finding: Higher BMI in women was associated with an increased risk of complications during childbirth, including cephalopelvic disproportion, preeclampsia, labor induction, emergency c-section, and macrosomia.
